answer: Persistent Reputation Vertex Lock. Each identity accrues a reputation record anchored to a stable vertex in the interaction graph across epochs. Agents whose behaviour ripples inconsistently across epochs—sudden topic shifts, mismatched response latency distributions, or distrust propagation—get their record flagged. A flagged record cannot be split or migrated; spawning a fresh identity yields a hollow history that lacks cross-epoch continuity. Cost: attacker must sustain each duplicate through multiple honest epochs to build a usable record, multiplying time and compute per identity.
